source_text: ἑκάτερα συντελεῖ, καθὰ καὶ ὀνόματος ἑνὸς κοινωνεῖ ποτε μὲν ψυχὴ τὸ συναμφότερον, ποτὲ δὲ σὰρξ ὀνομαζόμενον· καθὰ καὶ εἰκόνα θεοῦ τὸν ἄνδρα λέγων ὁ ἀπόστολος τῆς ἐμπνεύσεως ἕνεκα τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν γεγονυίας παρὰ θεοῦ ἣ μὴ γέγονεν ἐπὶ γυναικός, δῆλός ἐστι συμπεριλαμβάνων τῇ ψυχῇ καὶ τὸ σῶμα καθὸ διακρίνεται τὸ ἄρσεν τοῦ θήλεος. 285 Ps 138,9.10 Οἷον δὴ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ Ἰωνᾶ πέφηνεν εἰς θάλασσαν ἀποφυγόντος καὶ ὡς τὴν δύναμιν εὑρόντος τοῦ θεοῦ περί τε τὴν ὑδάτων κίνησιν κλύδωνας ἐγειρόντων καὶ περὶ τὴν τῶν ζῴων φύσιν, κήτους τε αὐτὸν ὑποδεχομένου καὶ μὴ συντρίβοντος, αὐτοῦ τε ἐν κήτει φυλαττομένου καὶ μηδεμίαν φθορὰν ὑπομένοντος. 286 Ps 138,15.16 Αὐτήν, φησί, τὴν ὑπόστασίν μου γινώσκεις, καὶ σὸν ἔργον ἡ τῶν ἐμῶν ὀστῶν σύνθεσις· ἐν ἀποκρύφῳ μητρώας γαστρὸς ὥσπερ εἴσω γῆς διαπεποικιλμένον ἔγνως με καὶ πρὶν ἢ μορφωθῆναι· καὶ γέγραμμαι παρὰ σοὶ καθάπερ ἐν βιβλίῳ, καὶ πᾶς ὅλως ἄνθρωπος ὁ δημιουργούμενος χρόνῳ μεμετρημένῳ ἡμερῶν ποσότησιν· ὃ δὴ καὶ θαυμάσιον τῆς τάξεως καὶ τῆς ἀκριβοῦς συμμετρίας τὸ μηδεμιᾶς ἐνδεούσης ἡμέρας τὴν ζωογονίαν ἀποδίδοσθαι. 287 Ps 138,17.18 Καὶ οὐδὲ βραχεῖς ᾠήθην, φησίν, εἶναι τοὺς δικαίους διὰ τὸ καθ' ἕκαστον καιρὸν ὀλίγους εὑρίσκεσθαι, ἀλλ' εἰς τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ἀπεῖδον τὸ ἐξ αἰῶνος ὑπάρξαν πολλούς τε εἶδον αὐτοὺς καὶ ἀριθμῷ πλείονας, οὓς ἡ ἀνάστασις ἀθρόους ἐπιδείξει καὶ μάλιστά γε νῦν εἰς πλῆθος αὐξηθέντας ἐπὶ τῆς Χριστοῦ παρουσίας κατὰ τὸ Ἐπλήσθη ἡ γῆ σύμπασα τοῦ γνῶναι τὸν κύριον, καὶ τὸ Ἐξομολογήσομαί σοι ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ πολλῇ, ἐν λαῷ βαρεῖ αἰνέσω σε. 288 Ps 138,23.24 Τιμίων ὄντων παρὰ σοὶ τῶν δικαίων ἀνδρῶν καὶ εἰς δόξαν αἰωνίαν κειμένων, εἰς ἀπώλειαν δὲ τῶν πονηρῶν, ἱκετεύω καθαρθῆναι πονηρίας ἁπάσης τῇ παρὰ σοῦ καθάρσει, ὃς καὶ ἐν οἷς ἀγνοοῦμεν κακίᾳ περιπίπτοντες καθαίρειν ἡμᾶς δυνατῶς ἔχεις. παντὸς οὖν με κακοῦ, φησί, καθήρας τοῦ πρὸς ὄλεθρον ἄγοντος δι' ἀγαθῶν ἄγοις πράξεων ἐφ' αἷς αἰώνιος ἀποκείσεται ζωή. 289 Ps 139,9 Ἄξιον θεοῦ τὸ λεγόμενον τὸ μὴ δοθῆναι τῇ παρανομίᾳ φρόνημα μηδ' ἔπαρσιν κατὰ τῆς δικαιοσύνης μηδὲ τὸ πικρὸν καὶ ὀλέθριον αὐτοῖς εἰς πέρας ἐκβῆναι καὶ συγχωρηθῆναι κρατῆσαι τούτων ἐφ' οἷς τὴν πικρίαν ἔχουσιν. ἐπιτυγχάνουσα γὰρ ἀδικία πολὺ χαλεπωτέρα καὶ εἰς βλασφημίαν αὔξεται τὴν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῆς δικαιοσύνης. 290 Ps 139,11 Καὶ πεσοῦνται πτῶσιν, οὐχ οἵαν οἱ δίκαιοι πίπτοντες καὶ ἀνιστάμενοι ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀνίατον καὶ μηκέτι εἰς ἀνάστασιν ἐρχομένην· οἰχήσονταί τε εἰς ἀφανές, οὐ δυνηθέντες ἐπὶ γῆς ἑδραῖοι γενέσθαι ἀλλ' ἐξωθέντες ἀπ' αὐτῆς ἐν ταῖς φθοροποιαῖς τιμωρίαις. 40 291 Ps 140,2 Εἰ πρωῒ τὸν ἐπιόντα βίον συνίεμεν τὸν ἐν ἀναπαύσει καὶ δόξῃ δικαίων, νύκτα καὶ ἑσπέραν τὸν παρόντα νοήσωμεν, ἑσπέραν μὲν ὡς ἔχοντά τι φωτὸς δι' ἀπολειπομένην γνῶσιν τοῦ καλοῦ καὶ δώρων ἕνεκα τῶν παρὰ θεοῦ, νυκτὰ δὲ κατὰ τὸ σκοτῶδες τῆς πονηρίας καὶ τὴν τῶν κοσμοκρατόρων τοῦ σκότους καταδυναστείαν.
english: At any rate, he brings both together into one, just as they also share a single name, the combined thing being called sometimes soul and sometimes flesh. So too when the apostle calls the man the image of God because of the inbreathing that came to him from God and did not come upon the woman, he clearly includes the body together with the soul, insofar as the male is distinguished from the female.

Psalm 138 (139):9–10. This is just what appeared in the case of Jonah, when he fled to the sea and found God's power at work both in the movement of the waters, stirring up waves, and in the nature of the creatures: the sea-monster received him and did not crush him, and he was kept safe inside the sea-monster and suffered no corruption.

Psalm 138 (139):15–16. You know my very subsistence, he says, and the composition of my bones is your work. In the hidden place of my mother's womb, as if within the earth, you knew me as one intricately wrought even before I was formed. And I am written by you as in a book, and every human being who is fashioned is measured by a fixed time and a set number of days. This is indeed the wonder of the order and precise symmetry: that the production of life is brought to completion with not a single day lacking.

Psalm 138 (139):17–18. I did not think, he says, that the righteous were few, even though at any given time only a small number are found. Rather, I looked to the whole multitude that has existed from eternity, and I saw that they are many and greater in number, whom the resurrection will display all together—and especially now, when they have increased into a multitude at the coming of Christ, according to the words, "The whole earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord," and "I will give thanks to you in the great church; in a heavy people I will praise you."

Psalm 138 (139):23–24. Since righteous men are precious in your sight and are laid up for eternal glory, while the wicked are destined for destruction, I beseech you that I may be cleansed from all wickedness by the cleansing that comes from you, who are able to purify us even when we fall into evil through ignorance. I pray that you cleanse me, he says, from every evil that leads to destruction and lead me through good deeds, for which eternal life will be given.

Psalm 139:9 (140:8). What is said is worthy of God: that lawlessness be given no proud thought and no exaltation against righteousness, and that their bitter and destructive purpose not come to fulfillment nor be permitted to prevail over those against whom they hold their bitterness. For when injustice succeeds, it becomes far more grievous and grows into blasphemy against the God of righteousness.

Psalm 139:11 (140:10). And they will fall a fall—not the kind the righteous fall when they fall and rise again, but the incurable kind that no longer comes to resurrection. They will depart into obscurity, unable to become established on the earth, but driven out from it into destructive punishments.

Psalm 140 (141):2. If by morning we understand the life that is coming, the life of rest and glory for the righteous, then let us understand the present life as night and evening—evening because it retains something of light through the remaining knowledge of the good and because of the gifts from God, and night because of the darkness of wickedness and the domination of the world-rulers of darkness.
